## Natural history notes

A large trap-jaw ant characterized by its dark reddish-brown to black body, long legs, powerful straight mandibles, and roughened node on the waist that helps distinguish it from similar species. In Florida, it is found in warm, humid habitats such as hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, gardens, yards, parks, and leaf litter or rotting wood where colonies can nest in soil, logs, or cavities. It is an active predator and scavenger, using its spring-loaded jaws to seize small insects and other arthropods, while also foraging for nectar, honeydew, and other sugary resources.
